name: TanStack
summary: A family of open-source TypeScript libraries (Query, Table, Form, Router, Start and more), each a framework-agnostic core with thin adapters, that handle state and logic while you keep the markup.
intro: TanStack Query manages server state: data that lives on a server, is fetched asynchronously and can change without your app knowing. You give it a key and a function that returns a promise, and it caches the result, merges identical requests into one, and refetches stale data in the background when a component mounts, the window regains focus or the network reconnects. By default cached data counts as stale immediately, failed queries retry 3 times with exponential backoff, and unused entries are garbage-collected after 5 minutes. TanStack Table is a headless engine for tables and data grids: it sorts, filters, groups and paginates rows but renders nothing, so you write the markup with any CSS or component library. Version 9 (August 2026) makes every feature opt-in for smaller bundles and, in TanStack’s own benchmark, retains up to 86% less JavaScript heap than v8. TanStack Form is a headless, type-safe form library with adapters for React, Vue, Angular, Solid, Svelte and Lit.

TanStack Router is a router for React and Solid whose types are inferred from your route definitions, so links, path params and validated search params are checked by the compiler; route loaders cache with stale-while-revalidate. TanStack Start is a full-stack React framework built on Router and Vite or Rsbuild, adding server-side rendering, streaming, server routes, server functions (type-safe RPCs between client and server) and middleware. As of October 2026 its docs still call Start a release candidate, with React Server Components experimental.

Each library keeps its logic in framework-agnostic TypeScript and connects it to a framework through an adapter: Table v9 ships ten adapters plus `@tanstack/table-core`. Tanner Linsley started the libraries at Nozzle, an earlier startup Linsley worked on, and has worked on TanStack full time since about November 2023. TanStack LLC is bootstrapped, with no venture funding; partner companies pay for the work. In November 2025 TanStack counted 13 active projects and 36 core contributors.
strengths: Query removes most hand-written fetching code: caching, request deduplication, background refetching, retries and garbage collection are defaults, tuned per query with options such as `staleTime` and `gcTime`
Framework-agnostic cores: Table’s logic runs under ten frameworks or in plain TypeScript, and Query’s `QueryClient` lives in a core shared by its framework adapters
Headless Table and Form fit any design system, from Tailwind to Material UI, because they never render markup of their own
Types inferred end to end in Router and Start: route paths, params and search params are typed from the route definitions
MIT-licensed and independent, funded by partner companies rather than investors
limits: Headless means more code: Table hands you rows and state, not a grid, so every header, cell and pagination control is yours to build and style; AG Grid or MUI X ship ready-made grids
Major versions break APIs: Query v5 removed call overloads and renamed `cacheTime` to `gcTime` and `loading` to `pending`, and Table v9 makes you declare each feature you use
Query’s defaults catch newcomers off guard, as its docs warn: data is stale at once and refetched on mount, focus and reconnect, and failures retry 3 times before the UI sees an error
Start is still a release candidate; a critical reflected XSS in its server-function handling (CVE-2026-102989) was patched on 30 September 2026

On 11 May 2026 an attacker used GitHub Actions cache poisoning to publish 84 malicious versions of 42 `@tanstack` Router and Start packages to npm; they were deprecated within the hour and other libraries were unaffected

story: TanStack grew out of a handful of libraries Tanner Linsley built at Nozzle, an earlier startup Linsley worked on, which had large amounts of marketing and SEO data to show. Two of them, React Table and React Query, carried the React name until the TanStack rename. React Table v7, released in March 2020 after more than a year of work, rebuilt it as a hooks-only, headless utility that renders no UI at all, so the library could stay small and leave the look of each table to the app.

In July 2022 React Query v4 was renamed TanStack Query and restructured as a monorepo with a framework-agnostic core and framework adapters, so the same caching engine could serve Vue, Svelte and Solid as well as React. Query v5 followed in October 2023, after 91 alphas, 35 betas and 16 release candidates, and Router reached 1.0 in December 2023. Around then Tanner went full time on TanStack, paid for by partner companies rather than investors.

Form v1 shipped in March 2025 with five framework adapters, and Start, a full-stack framework on Router, reached a release candidate in September 2025. In May 2026 an attacker chained a `pull_request_target` workflow, GitHub Actions cache poisoning and an OIDC token read from runner memory to publish malicious Router and Start versions, and TanStack published a detailed postmortem. Table v9 arrived in August 2026, after more than two years of on-and-off work.

choices.why: React Table v7’s release notes argued that the look of a table belongs to the app, that dropping UI options removes a huge API surface to maintain, and that apps can then extend it however they like.

choices.choice: Treat server state apart from client state
choices.why: Query’s docs note that server state is stored remotely, needs async APIs, is shared with other people and goes out of date, which general client-state stores don’t handle; caching, deduplication and background updates follow from that.

choices.choice: One agnostic core, thin framework adapters
choices.why: Query v4 moved the `QueryClient` and subscriptions into a shared core so hooks like `useQuery` became a small React layer, and the same logic could serve other frameworks.
Router is designed so TypeScript knows every route’s path, params, search params and context, making a link to a route that doesn’t exist a compile error rather than a runtime 404.

timeline.text: React Table v7, a headless, hooks-only rewrite, in March
React Query v4 becomes TanStack Query, with a framework-agnostic core
Query v5 in October; Router 1.0 in December
Form v1 in March; Start release candidate in September
npm supply-chain attack on Router and Start packages in May
Table v9 with opt-in features and ten framework adapters in August
